description: Graph predicates, size and degree measures, distance-based measures (diameter, radius, eccentricity, centre), clustering and assortativity, additional centralities, cliques/covers/cuts/connectivity, colouring, isomorphism and automorphisms, and the graph-operation algebra (complement, unions, products, contraction, line graphs, transitive closure).

tools.name: GraphQ
tools.description: Basic graph predicates: GraphQ (is a Graph object), DirectedGraphQ, UndirectedGraphQ, MixedGraphQ, WeightedGraphQ, SimpleGraphQ (no loops or multi-edges), MultigraphQ, LoopFreeGraphQ, EmptyGraphQ, CompleteGraphQ and PathGraphQ; VertexQ[g, v] and EdgeQ[g, e] test membership. Use them to validate inputs and choose algorithms.
tools.usage:
GraphQ[g]
DirectedGraphQ[g]
WeightedGraphQ[g]
SimpleGraphQ[g]
CompleteGraphQ[g]
VertexQ[g, v]
EdgeQ[g, v -> w]
tools.example:
g = Graph[{1 -> 2, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 1}];
{DirectedGraphQ[g], SimpleGraphQ[g], EdgeQ[g, 1 -> 2], VertexQ[g, 5]} (* {True, True, True, False} *)

tools.name: ConnectedGraphQ
tools.description: Structural predicates: ConnectedGraphQ (WeaklyConnectedGraphQ / StronglyConnectedGraphQ for directed graphs), AcyclicGraphQ, TreeGraphQ, BipartiteGraphQ, PlanarGraphQ, EulerianGraphQ, HamiltonianGraphQ, VertexTransitiveGraphQ and EdgeTransitiveGraphQ. Cheap to evaluate and useful as guards before running expensive algorithms.
tools.usage:
ConnectedGraphQ[g]
WeaklyConnectedGraphQ[g]
StronglyConnectedGraphQ[g]
AcyclicGraphQ[g]
TreeGraphQ[g]
BipartiteGraphQ[g]
PlanarGraphQ[g]
EulerianGraphQ[g]
HamiltonianGraphQ[g]
tools.example:
PlanarGraphQ[CompleteGraph[5]] (* False *)
BipartiteGraphQ[CycleGraph[6]] (* True *)
AcyclicGraphQ[Graph[{1 -> 2, 2 -> 3}]] (* True *)

tools.name: VertexCount
tools.description: VertexCount and EdgeCount give the number of vertices/edges (optionally matching a pattern); VertexInDegree and VertexOutDegree give in/out degrees for directed graphs (VertexDegree is already listed). Fundamental size measures used in density, normalisation and reporting.
tools.usage:
VertexCount[g]
VertexCount[g, patt]
EdgeCount[g]
EdgeCount[g, patt]
VertexInDegree[g]
VertexInDegree[g, v]
VertexOutDegree[g]

parameters.name: patt
parameters.description: Pattern restricting counted vertices/edges, e.g. _ -> 3 for edges into vertex 3.

tools.name: GraphDiameter
tools.description: Distance-based global measures: GraphDiameter (longest shortest path), GraphRadius (minimum eccentricity), VertexEccentricity (max distance from a vertex), GraphCenter (vertices of minimum eccentricity), GraphPeriphery (vertices of maximum eccentricity), MeanGraphDistance and GraphDistanceMatrix (all-pairs distances). Edge weights are used when present.
tools.usage:
GraphDiameter[g]
GraphRadius[g]
VertexEccentricity[g, v]
GraphCenter[g]
GraphPeriphery[g]
MeanGraphDistance[g]
GraphDistanceMatrix[g]
tools.example:
g = GridGraph[{5, 5}];
{GraphDiameter[g], GraphRadius[g]} (* {8, 4} *)
GraphCenter[g] (* {13} *)
MatrixPlot[GraphDistanceMatrix[g]]

tools.name: GlobalClusteringCoefficient
tools.description: Clustering measures: GlobalClusteringCoefficient (fraction of closed triplets / transitivity), LocalClusteringCoefficient (per vertex), MeanClusteringCoefficient (average of local values); GraphAssortativity measures degree (or property) correlation between adjacent vertices and GraphDensity the edge density. Standard descriptors in network science and small-world analysis.
tools.usage:
GlobalClusteringCoefficient[g]
LocalClusteringCoefficient[g]
LocalClusteringCoefficient[g, v]
MeanClusteringCoefficient[g]
GraphAssortativity[g]
GraphAssortativity[g, {{v1, v2, ...}, ...}]
GraphDensity[g]

tools.name: KatzCentrality
tools.description: Additional centrality measures: KatzCentrality (attenuated walk counts with parameter alpha), HITSCentrality (hub and authority scores), EdgeBetweennessCentrality (betweenness of edges, used in Girvan-Newman community detection), RadialityCentrality, StatusCentrality and LinkRankCentrality (edge PageRank). All return lists in VertexList/EdgeList order.
tools.usage:
KatzCentrality[g, alpha]
KatzCentrality[g, alpha, beta]
HITSCentrality[g]
EdgeBetweennessCentrality[g]
RadialityCentrality[g]
StatusCentrality[g]
LinkRankCentrality[g, alpha]

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Attenuation factor (must be below 1/largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix for Katz).

tools.name: VertexJaccardSimilarity
tools.description: Vertex similarity measures based on neighbourhoods: VertexJaccardSimilarity, VertexDiceSimilarity, VertexCosineSimilarity and VertexCorrelationSimilarity give the similarity of two vertices (or the full matrix), used for link prediction and role analysis; MeanNeighborDegree and MeanDegreeConnectivity describe degree correlations.
tools.usage:
VertexJaccardSimilarity[g, u, v]
VertexJaccardSimilarity[g]
VertexCosineSimilarity[g, u, v]
VertexDiceSimilarity[g]
MeanNeighborDegree[g]
MeanDegreeConnectivity[g]

parameters.name: u, v
parameters.description: Vertices (omit for the full similarity matrix).

tools.name: FindClique
tools.description: Finds a largest clique (or n cliques, or cliques of given size) in a graph; FindKClique, FindKClan, FindKClub and FindKPlex find relaxed cohesive subgroups, and KCoreComponents gives k-cores. Cliques are NP-hard in general but practical for moderate graphs; use them for community and cohesion analysis.
tools.usage:
FindClique[g]
FindClique[g, n]
FindClique[g, {k}]
FindClique[g, {kmin, kmax}, All]
FindKClique[g, k]
FindKPlex[g, k]
KCoreComponents[g, k]

parameters.name: n / k
parameters.description: Number of cliques, or size specification.

tools.example:
g = ExampleData[{"NetworkGraph", "ZacharyKarateClub"}];
FindClique[g] (* a maximum clique *)
FindClique[g, {3}, All] // Length (* number of triangles' vertex sets *)
HighlightGraph[g, Subgraph[g, First[FindClique[g]]]]

tools.name: FindIndependentVertexSet
tools.description: Finds a maximum independent vertex set (no two adjacent), FindVertexCover a minimum vertex cover (its complement), FindIndependentEdgeSet a maximum matching and FindEdgeCover a minimum edge cover. These classical NP-hard/polynomial problems underlie scheduling, assignment and resource-allocation models on graphs.
tools.usage:
FindIndependentVertexSet[g]
FindIndependentVertexSet[g, {k}]
FindVertexCover[g]
FindIndependentEdgeSet[g]
FindEdgeCover[g]
tools.example:
g = PetersenGraph[];
FindIndependentVertexSet[g] (* 4 vertices *)
matching = FindIndependentEdgeSet[g]; Length[matching] (* 5: perfect matching *)
HighlightGraph[g, matching]
tools.notes: For weighted bipartite matching use FindMaximumFlow / LinearOptimization or FindIndependentEdgeSet on a weighted graph.

tools.name: FindEdgeCut
tools.description: FindEdgeCut finds a smallest set of edges whose removal disconnects the graph (or separates s from t), FindVertexCut the analogous vertex set and FindMinimumCut a minimum-weight cut with its partition; EdgeConnectivity and VertexConnectivity give the corresponding sizes. Used for reliability analysis and bottleneck detection.
tools.usage:
FindEdgeCut[g]
FindEdgeCut[g, s, t]
FindVertexCut[g]
FindVertexCut[g, s, t]
FindMinimumCut[g]
FindMinimumCut[g, s, t]
EdgeConnectivity[g]
VertexConnectivity[g]
tools.example:
g = GridGraph[{4, 4}];
EdgeConnectivity[g] (* 2 *)
FindEdgeCut[g, 1, 16]
{value, {a, b}} = FindMinimumCut[g, 1, 16]

tools.name: FindVertexColoring
tools.description: Finds a proper vertex colouring with the minimum (or a given) number of colours, FindEdgeColoring a proper edge colouring and FindPlanarColoring a colouring of the faces of a planar graph; VertexChromaticNumber, EdgeChromaticNumber and ChromaticPolynomial give the corresponding invariants. Applications: register allocation, timetabling, frequency assignment.
tools.usage:
FindVertexColoring[g]
FindVertexColoring[g, k]
FindVertexColoring[g, {c1, c2, ...}]
FindEdgeColoring[g]
VertexChromaticNumber[g]
EdgeChromaticNumber[g]
ChromaticPolynomial[g, x]

tools.name: FindGraphIsomorphism
tools.description: Finds an explicit vertex mapping between isomorphic graphs (or All mappings); FindSubgraphIsomorphism / IsomorphicSubgraphQ / FindIsomorphicSubgraph handle subgraph isomorphism, CanonicalGraph gives a canonical form usable as a hash key for isomorphism classes, and GraphAutomorphismGroup the symmetry group. Use them for pattern matching in molecular and circuit graphs.
tools.usage:
FindGraphIsomorphism[g1, g2]
FindGraphIsomorphism[g1, g2, All]
FindSubgraphIsomorphism[g1, g2]
IsomorphicSubgraphQ[g1, g2]
CanonicalGraph[g]
GraphAutomorphismGroup[g]

parameters.name: g1, g2
parameters.description: Graphs (g1 is matched into g2 for subgraph forms).

tools.example:
FindGraphIsomorphism[CycleGraph[4], Graph[{a <-> b, b <-> c, c <-> d, d <-> a}]]
GroupOrder[GraphAutomorphismGroup[PetersenGraph[]]] (* 120 *)
DeleteDuplicatesBy[graphs, CanonicalGraph] (* one representative per isomorphism class *)

tools.name: WeaklyConnectedComponents
tools.description: WeaklyConnectedComponents gives the vertex sets of weakly connected components of a directed graph (ConnectedComponents gives strongly connected ones for directed graphs), ConnectedGraphComponents returns the components as graphs, and KCoreComponents the k-core subgraphs. WeaklyConnectedGraphComponents is the graph-returning weak form.
tools.usage:
WeaklyConnectedComponents[g]
WeaklyConnectedGraphComponents[g]
ConnectedGraphComponents[g]
KCoreComponents[g]
KCoreComponents[g, k]

tools.name: BreadthFirstScan
tools.description: Performs a breadth-first (BreadthFirstScan) or depth-first (DepthFirstScan) traversal from a start vertex, calling user functions at events such as "DiscoverVertex", "VisitedVertex", "FrontierEdge", "TreeEdge", "BackEdge", "CrossEdge", "UnvisitedVertex"; the return value is the list of discovery-order vertices. Use them to implement custom graph algorithms (level assignment, cycle detection, ordering).
tools.usage:
BreadthFirstScan[g, v, {"event1" -> f1, "event2" -> f2, ...}]
DepthFirstScan[g, v, {"DiscoverVertex" -> f, "BackEdge" -> g}]
BreadthFirstScan[g, v]

parameters.name: event -> f
parameters.description: Handler functions receiving vertex (and parent/distance) or edge arguments.

tools.name: FindPostmanTour
tools.description: Finds a Chinese-postman tour: a shortest closed walk traversing every edge at least once (Eulerian circuit if one exists). Together with FindHamiltonianPath, FindEulerianCycle (listed) and FindShortestTour it covers the classic route-inspection problems for street sweeping, plotting and inspection.
tools.usage:
FindPostmanTour[g]
FindPostmanTour[g, k]
FindHamiltonianPath[g]
FindHamiltonianPath[g, s, t]

tools.name: FindPath
tools.description: Finds paths between two vertices: FindPath[g, s, t] one path, FindPath[g, s, t, kspec, n] n paths of length in kspec (All for all simple paths); FindEdgeIndependentPaths and FindVertexIndependentPaths find disjoint path families (Menger's theorem). Complement to FindShortestPath when alternatives or all routes are needed.
tools.usage:
FindPath[g, s, t]
FindPath[g, s, t, kspec]
FindPath[g, s, t, kspec, n]
FindPath[g, s, t, Infinity, All]
FindEdgeIndependentPaths[g, s, t]
FindVertexIndependentPaths[g, s, t, k]

parameters.name: kspec
parameters.description: Path length bound: k, {kmin, kmax} or Infinity.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of paths (All for every one).

tools.name: GraphComplement
tools.description: Graph algebra: GraphComplement (edges between non-adjacent vertices), GraphUnion / GraphIntersection / GraphDifference (edge-set operations on shared vertices), GraphDisjointUnion (relabelled disjoint copies), GraphSum and GraphJoin (union plus all edges between the two vertex sets). Use them to build graphs compositionally.
tools.usage:
GraphComplement[g]
GraphUnion[g1, g2, ...]
GraphIntersection[g1, g2]
GraphDifference[g1, g2]
GraphDisjointUnion[g1, g2, ...]
GraphSum[g1, g2]
GraphJoin[g1, g2]
tools.example:
GraphComplement[CycleGraph[5]] (* another 5-cycle *)
GraphJoin[CompleteGraph[1], CycleGraph[6]] (* wheel graph *)
IsomorphicGraphQ[%, WheelGraph[7]]

tools.name: GraphProduct
tools.description: Graph products with the standard types "Cartesian" (default), "Tensor", "Strong", "Lexicographical", "Conormal" and others, plus GraphPower (connect vertices within distance k). Cartesian products build grids, tori and hypercubes from paths and cycles; powers model k-hop reachability.
tools.usage:
GraphProduct[g1, g2]
GraphProduct[g1, g2, "type"]
GraphPower[g, k]
tools.example:
IsomorphicGraphQ[GraphProduct[PathGraph[Range[3]], PathGraph[Range[4]]], GridGraph[{3, 4}]] (* True *)
GraphPower[PathGraph[Range[6]], 2]

tools.name: LineGraph
tools.description: Constructs the line graph (vertices = edges of g, adjacent when they share an endpoint); DualPlanarGraph gives the planar dual (faces become vertices) and PlanarFaceList the faces of a planar embedding. Line graphs turn edge problems (edge colouring, edge cover) into vertex problems.
tools.usage:
LineGraph[g]
DualPlanarGraph[g]
PlanarFaceList[g]
tools.example:
LineGraph[StarGraph[5]] (* K4 *)
DualPlanarGraph[GridGraph[{3, 3}]]
PlanarFaceList[CycleGraph[4]]

tools.name: EdgeContract
tools.description: EdgeContract merges the endpoints of an edge (or edges) into one vertex, VertexContract merges a set of vertices, VertexReplace renames vertices by rules and VertexAdd inserts vertices; with EdgeAdd/EdgeDelete/VertexDelete (listed) they form the graph-editing toolkit used in coarsening, minor testing and Karger-style algorithms.
tools.usage:
EdgeContract[g, e]
EdgeContract[g, {e1, e2, ...}]
VertexContract[g, {v1, v2, ...}]
VertexReplace[g, {v1 -> w1, ...}]
VertexAdd[g, v]
VertexAdd[g, {v1, v2, ...}]

tools.name: ReverseGraph
tools.description: ReverseGraph reverses all edge directions, DirectedGraph converts an undirected graph to directed ("Acyclic", "Random" or both directions) and UndirectedGraph drops directions; IndexGraph relabels vertices 1..n and SimpleGraph removes loops and multi-edges. Common normalisation steps before algorithms that require a particular graph type.
tools.usage:
ReverseGraph[g]
DirectedGraph[g]
DirectedGraph[g, "Acyclic"]
UndirectedGraph[g]
IndexGraph[g]
IndexGraph[g, n]
SimpleGraph[g]

tools.name: TransitiveClosureGraph
tools.description: TransitiveClosureGraph adds an edge u -> w whenever w is reachable from u; TransitiveReductionGraph removes edges implied by others (minimal equivalent DAG, e.g. Hasse diagrams). Both are essential for reachability queries, dependency graphs and partial-order visualisation.
tools.usage:
TransitiveClosureGraph[g]
TransitiveReductionGraph[g]

tools.name: EdgeTaggedGraph
tools.description: Creates a graph whose edges carry tags (DirectedEdge[u, v, tag]) so that multi-edges with different labels are distinguishable; EdgeTags lists the tags and EdgeTaggedGraphQ tests for the form. Used for multigraphs with typed relations (knowledge graphs, transport modes).
tools.usage:
EdgeTaggedGraph[{u1 -> v1, ...}]
EdgeTaggedGraph[{DirectedEdge[u, v, tag], ...}]
EdgeTags[g]
EdgeTaggedGraphQ[g]
IndexEdgeTaggedGraph[g]
tools.example:
g = EdgeTaggedGraph[{DirectedEdge["A", "B", "bus"], DirectedEdge["A", "B", "train"]}, EdgeLabels -> "EdgeTag"];
EdgeTags[g]

tools.name: BooleanGraph
tools.description: Combines graphs with a Boolean function on their edge sets (BooleanGraph[Xor, g1, g2] keeps edges in exactly one graph), generalizing union/intersection/difference on the shared vertex set. Handy for comparing network snapshots.
tools.usage: BooleanGraph[f, g1, g2, ...]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Boolean function applied to edge membership, e.g. And, Or, Xor, or a custom function.

tools.example: changed = BooleanGraph[Xor, networkDay1, networkDay2]; EdgeCount[changed]

tools.name: DominatorTreeGraph
tools.description: Computes the dominator tree of a directed graph from a root (u dominates v if every path from the root to v passes through u); DominatorVertexList gives the dominator list for a vertex. Used in compiler control-flow analysis and network vulnerability studies.
tools.usage:
DominatorTreeGraph[g, r]
DominatorVertexList[g, r]
DominatorVertexList[g, r, v]
tools.example:
cfg = Graph[{1 -> 2, 2 -> 3, 2 -> 4, 3 -> 5, 4 -> 5, 5 -> 2}];
DominatorTreeGraph[cfg, 1]

tools.name: FindGraphPartition
tools.description: Partitions the vertices of a graph into k (default 2) balanced parts minimising the number (or weight) of cut edges, with optional part sizes; a spectral/multilevel alternative to FindGraphCommunities for load balancing, circuit placement and parallel mesh decomposition.
tools.usage:
FindGraphPartition[g]
FindGraphPartition[g, k]
FindGraphPartition[g, {n1, n2, ...}]

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of parts, or explicit part sizes.

tools.name: FindMinimumCostFlow
tools.description: Solves the minimum-cost flow problem on a graph with EdgeCost and EdgeCapacity (and optional supplies/demands or a required flow value), returning the cost or, with a property, the "FlowGraph", "EdgeList", "FlowMatrix" or an "OptimumFlowData" object; FindMaximumFlow (listed) accepts the same property arguments ("FlowValue", "FlowGraph", "SourceCut", "SinkCut"). Used for transportation, assignment and routing problems.
tools.usage:
FindMinimumCostFlow[g, s, t]
FindMinimumCostFlow[g, s, t, d]
FindMinimumCostFlow[g, {b1, b2, ...}]
FindMinimumCostFlow[g, s, t, "OptimumFlowData"]
FindMaximumFlow[g, s, t, "FlowGraph"]

parameters.name: s, t
parameters.description: Source and sink; or a supply/demand vector b.

tools.name: VertexComponent
tools.description: VertexComponent[g, {v1, ...}] gives all vertices reachable from (or connected to) the given vertices - the reachability set - and EdgeComponent the corresponding edges; VertexInComponent/VertexOutComponent restrict to in/out reachability in directed graphs. Cheaper than computing all components when only one seed matters.
tools.usage:
VertexComponent[g, {v1, v2, ...}]
VertexComponent[g, v, k] (* within distance k *)
VertexOutComponent[g, v]
VertexInComponent[g, v]
EdgeComponent[g, {v1, ...}]

tools.name: GraphHub
tools.description: GraphHub gives the vertices of maximum degree (with an optional count) and GraphLinkEfficiency measures how efficiently a graph connects vertices relative to its distances; GraphReciprocity is the fraction of reciprocated directed edges. Simple descriptive statistics for network reports.
tools.usage:
GraphHub[g]
GraphHub[g, k]
GraphLinkEfficiency[g]
GraphReciprocity[g]
